subject: Physics
scope_summary: Imported candidate for 1D & 2D Kinematics & Projectile Motion. No authority is carried; every gap below must be authored before this can be admitted.

microtopics.title: 1D & 2D Kinematics & Projectile Motion
entry_assumptions: **Constant Acceleration Constraint**: The kinematic equations ($v = u + at$, $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$, $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$) hold **if and only if** acceleration is strictly constant ($\vec{a} = \text{const}$). For time-varying or position-dependent acceleration, calculus definitions $v = \frac{ds}{dt}$ and $a = v\frac{dv}{ds}$ must be integrated.
**Independence of Orthogonal Motions**: In 2D projectile motion, the horizontal ($x$) and vertical ($y$) components are completely independent and coupled only by time parameter $t$.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Distinction between distance (scalar path length) and displacement (vector $\Delta \vec{r} = \vec{r}_f - \vec{r}_i$).

teaching_path.action: Projectile trajectory equation in vacuum: $y = x\tan\theta - \frac{g x^2}{2 u^2 \cos^2\theta} = x\tan\theta\left(1 - \frac{x}{R}\right)$.
Resolving relative motion in 2D: $\vec{v}_{A/B} = \vec{v}_A - \vec{v}_B$ (rain-umbrella, river-swimmer problems).

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Saying a ball thrown vertically upward has $a = 0$ at its highest point because $v = 0$.
misconceptions.repair: At the peak, velocity is instantaneously zero ($v = 0$), but acceleration is constant and non-zero ($a = -g = -9.8\text{ m/s}^2$).

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Calculating average speed for round trip at speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$ as arithmetic mean $\frac{v_1+v_2}{2}$.
misconceptions.repair: Average speed is total distance over total time: $v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}$ (harmonic mean).
